h: Winning ways and Steel City sights
p: The secret to escaping isn't being a genius. It's teamwork, a good search and a willingness to say silly ideas out loud. Spread out at the start and give the room a thorough going-over, then pool everything in one place where everyone can see it. When something doesn't make sense, talk it through as a group. One person's half-idea often sparks someone else's breakthrough. And if you're truly stuck, take a hint without feeling guilty.

Sheffield is a big student city, so escape rooms are popular for socials and birthdays. They're also a great option for families on a wet weekend, especially with teens who'd rather be anywhere than another shop. Turn up a few minutes before your slot so the briefing isn't rushed, and leave big bags and coats somewhere sensible so your hands are free to rummage. It makes a real difference once the clock is running.

The city's Supertram makes getting about easy, and Sheffield station is a short walk from the centre, with the stainless steel Cutting Edge sculpture in Sheaf Square a fitting welcome to the Steel City. Once you've escaped, there's lots to see. The Millennium Gallery, next to the Winter Garden, celebrates Sheffield's metalwork heritage alongside changing exhibitions. Theatre lovers have the Crucible and the Lyceum side by side, the Crucible being world-famous as the home of snooker's World Championship. Kelham Island Museum tells the city's industrial story, and the area around it is buzzing with independent pubs and eateries. For a calmer afternoon, the Sheffield Botanical Gardens are beautiful, and the Peak District is right on the doorstep, with spots like Padley Gorge and Stanage Edge within easy reach.
